screens_reviewed: Two scroll captures of app/(tabs)/index.tsx (Dashboard) in dark theme: 03-home.png (top — header, status/offline cards, metric grid, mint workflow card) and 04-home-assigned-places.png (scrolled — Assigned places list with Submitted/Not started cards).
verdict: A well-composed dashboard that renders the warm dark palette correctly (background #141513, mint primary #7FBFA3, muted surfaces) and consistently uses the shared ScaledText/ScaledParagraph primitives, matching design_system_components_used. The main concern is safe-area handling: the screen relies on a fixed Stack paddingTop:20 plus ScrollView contentInsetAdjustmentBehavior rather than passing the live top inset into its content container, so the header crowds the status bar/Dynamic Island. A couple of small spacing/token issues round out an otherwise solid screen.

critical_issues.location: app/(tabs)/index.tsx ScrollView contentContainerStyle (lines 115-118); app/_layout.tsx Stack contentStyle (lines 1376-1379)
critical_issues.issue: The dashboard does not consume useSafeAreaInsets().top. getResponsiveContentContainerStyle is called without a topInset, so vertical clearance above the 'Active auditor' header comes only from the root Stack's fixed paddingTop:20 plus ScrollView contentInsetAdjustmentBehavior="automatic". On a Dynamic Island / notch device this fixed 20px is not the real inset, and in the screenshot the avatar/'Active auditor' row sits tight under the status bar with little breathing room.
critical_issues.evidence: image 03-home.png (header hugging status bar); index.tsx:115-118 (no topInset passed); _layout.tsx:1378 (paddingTop: 20 hardcoded); responsive-layout.ts:758-762 (topInset path exists but unused)
critical_issues.fix: Call const insets = useSafeAreaInsets() in DashboardScreen and pass topInset: insets.top (with includeTopPadding) to getResponsiveContentContainerStyle, or wrap content in a SafeAreaView edges={['top']}; drop the fixed paddingTop:20 on the root Stack so each screen owns its real inset.

improvements.suggestion: paddingTop is computed as tabBarLayout.paddingTop - 10, which on phone is 8 - 10 = -2 (a negative padding). It happens to render acceptably in the screenshot, but a negative padding is fragile and can clip the icon/label on RN version bumps. Use a non-negative value (e.g. Math.max(0, paddingTop - 10) or just a tuned constant).

MetricCard sets width="48%" together with minWidth:160. On the narrowest phones (e.g. ~320pt content width) 48% can fall below 160, forcing the wrap to break to one column. On the captured device it renders as a clean 2x2 grid, but consider deriving the width from layout tokens or using a flexBasis so the 2-up grid is guaranteed across phone widths.
improvements.evidence: index.tsx:606-607 (width "48%" + minWidth 160); image 03-home.png (2x2 grid renders correctly here)

improvements.suggestion: The mint 'Your assigned places' card hardcodes literal rgba whites (rgba(255,255,255,0.78), rgba(255,255,255,0.1)/0.16) and a one-off borderColor rgba(71,203,175,0.18) instead of palette tokens. This bypasses the dark/light design-system tokens and the secondary action buttons read as very low-contrast translucent fills on the mint surface (visible in 03-home.png). Prefer tokens (e.g. primaryForeground with controlled opacity / a defined onPrimary token) so contrast is consistent across themes.
improvements.evidence: index.tsx:314,322,339,665,671 (literal rgba values); image 03-home.png (secondary buttons faint on mint card)

tamagui_notes: Screen correctly imports ScaledParagraph/ScaledText from components/ui and aliases them as Paragraph/Text (index.tsx:25), matching design_system_components_used and ensuring numeric fontSize/lineHeight scale with the fontScale preference (ScaledText.tsx:2285-2321). No hand-rolled raw Tamagui Text/Paragraph for body copy.

Dark palette is applied via useDesignSystem()/getDesignSystem (design-system.ts:342-375): background #141513, surface #1E201C, primary #7FBFA3, warning #E0B873, success #7FBFA3 — all consistent with the rendered screenshots.

Spacing mixes design-system tokens with Tamagui scale tokens: outer container uses fixed bottomPadding:132 and gap:28 (index.tsx:116-117) while inner stacks use $-scale gaps ($6, $3, $2.5). Not a bug, but the magic 132/28 could be derived from layout tokens for consistency.
radii are taken from designSystem.radii (md/lg/button/full) rather than ad-hoc numbers — good token discipline (e.g. index.tsx:128,212,441).
platform_notes: iPhone safe-area: the home indicator region is handled by the tab bar paddingBottom (8 + insets.bottom via getResponsiveTabBarLayout, responsive-layout.ts:710), so the bottom edge clears the indicator. The TOP inset, however, is not wired into this screen (see critical issue).

Thumb reach: the primary CTAs live inside the mint workflow card mid-screen and the per-place Start/Continue/View report buttons sit on the right edge of each card — all within comfortable thumb range; the only top-of-screen controls (refresh/settings, 42x42) are secondary, which is fine.
Tap targets: header icon buttons are 42x42 (index.tsx:157-158,177-178) — slightly under the 44pt iOS guideline but close; per-place action buttons use Button size="$3" which renders adequately.
not_assessable: Exact top-inset overlap on a real Dynamic Island device (the screenshot is a simulator capture; clearance looks tight but is not provably clipped).
Loading/empty/error runtime states (Spinner, EmptyStateCard, errorMessage banner) are not shown in either capture.
Precise WCAG contrast ratios for the translucent white text/buttons on the mint card (estimated only).
Pressed/focus visuals for buttons (pressStyle) cannot be judged from static captures.
score_rationale: Solid, on-platform dark dashboard with correct palette, consistent use of the shared ScaledText/ScaledParagraph primitives, and good token discipline for color/radii. Held back from 9 by one real safe-area gap (top inset not consumed; fixed paddingTop:20) and minor polish items (negative tab-bar paddingTop, hardcoded rgba on the mint card, 48%/minWidth metric grid) — minor polish rather than significant problems.
